skill.name: backend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Guides Node.js, Express, and TypeScript backend development with layered architecture. Covers Prisma, Zod, Sentry, middleware, configuration, async errors, testing, and legacy refactoring.
skill.summary: Build consistent TypeScript backend services with layered architecture and reusable implementation patterns.
skill.author: BrianDai22

security_audit.summary: All 214 static matches are false positives caused by Markdown, imports, template literals, fixed paths, placeholders, and defensive configuration guidance. No malicious intent, prompt injection, reconnaissance, shell execution, or arbitrary file access was found. Two high-impact guidance issues remain: an unsafe session-secret fallback and overly broad Sentry data collection.

remediation.issue: The configuration example uses a fixed fallback for the session secret.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the fallback, require a cryptographically random secret, and fail startup when the secret is missing in every deployed environment.

remediation.issue: The Sentry template captures more request and runtime data than most services need.
remediation.suggestion: Disable local-variable and broad request capture by default. Allowlist required fields and scrub secrets and personal data before transmission.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Default Session Secret
semantic_findings.description: The recommended configuration falls back to the fixed value dev-secret. A deployed service without explicit configuration could permit session forgery.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The recommended implementation directly uses a known session-secret fallback without an environment guard. Nearby text only labels defaults as development values.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Monitoring Data Collection
semantic_findings.description: The Sentry template collects local variables, request bodies, headers, IP addresses, query strings, and user identifiers. Limited scrubbing may expose secrets and personal data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template explicitly enables broad request and local-variable capture. Its scrubber removes two headers and masks one email field, leaving other sensitive fields unaddressed.

content.value_statement: Backend teams often produce inconsistent Express services with weak separation, validation, and error handling. This skill supplies reusable architecture, configuration, Prisma, Sentry, Zod, middleware, and testing guidance.
actual_capabilities: Structures Express services into routes, controllers, services, and repositories.
Provides TypeScript patterns for dependency injection, async errors, and reusable controllers.
Shows Prisma query, transaction, repository, and testing patterns.
Guides Zod validation, DTO design, and consistent error responses.
Covers middleware ordering, authentication context, Sentry monitoring, configuration, and test design.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not execute code or inspect runtime behavior.
Assumes Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Zod, and Sentry conventions.
Uses project-specific names and paths that require adaptation.
Security-sensitive defaults and telemetry settings require production review.

use_cases.title: Create a Backend Feature
use_cases.description: Plan a new endpoint across routing, validation, controller, service, repository, monitoring, and tests.

use_cases.title: Standardize a Service Team
use_cases.description: Establish shared TypeScript patterns for architecture, configuration, middleware, errors, and database access.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Routes
use_cases.description: Move business and database logic from large Express routes into testable layers.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a TypeScript Express endpoint for [feature]. Identify its route, validation schema, controller, service, repository needs, error handling, and tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a small backend feature.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [route file or description] using these backend guidelines. Propose a layered refactor and explain each responsibility change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when business logic has accumulated in route handlers.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Microservice
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript microservice for [domain]. Define its directories, middleware order, configuration, Prisma access, validation, monitoring, and test strategy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when creating a service with several endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [feature or service] against the complete guidelines. Prioritize architecture, authorization, validation, secret handling, telemetry privacy, error propagation, database efficiency, and coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced readiness review before deployment.

output_examples.input: Plan a user creation endpoint with Prisma and Zod.
output: Route: validate the request and delegate to the user controller.
Controller: map the validated request and return a consistent created response.
Service: enforce uniqueness and business rules through injected dependencies.
Repository: perform the Prisma create operation and translate database errors.
Tests: cover success, invalid input, duplicate email, and repository failure.

output_examples.input: Review an Express route that contains database queries and error formatting.
output: Move request handling and response formatting into a controller.
Move business decisions into a service.
Move repeated Prisma access into a repository.
Apply shared validation and error middleware at the route boundary.

output_examples.input: Outline a production readiness review for a notification service.
output_examples.output: Review middleware order, configuration validation, secret handling, request schemas, retry behavior, Sentry privacy, database transactions, health checks, and integration tests.

best_practices: Adapt examples to the repository patterns and verify every referenced dependency.
Require validation, authorization, error handling, and tests for every endpoint.
Review secret defaults and monitoring fields before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not place business logic or direct database access in route handlers.
Do not copy project-specific paths, credentials, or telemetry settings unchanged.
Do not treat example code as production-ready without security and integration review.

faq.question: Which backend stack does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Node.js services using Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Zod, and Sentry.

faq.question: Can it generate a complete service?
faq.answer: It can guide the structure and implementation, but repository-specific dependencies and deployment settings still need verification.

faq.question: Does it replace framework documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use current framework documentation for API changes, version compatibility, and deployment requirements.

faq.question: Can I use it without Prisma?
faq.answer: Yes. Keep the layered architecture and replace repository examples with your data-access library.

faq.question: Does it cover security?
faq.answer: It covers validation, authentication middleware, secret handling, and error boundaries. Production code still requires a dedicated security review.

faq.question: How should I use the examples?
faq.answer: Treat them as adaptable patterns. Confirm paths, types, authorization rules, secrets, telemetry fields, and tests in your repository.
